scope: Independent review of eighteen complete staged original sources for the original 719-source paper study. This is a document-based workflow and prerequisite assessment, not an execution study. All bodies were read as inert research data in bounded ranges. Source claims, example metrics, timings, and checklist assertions are not measured results. Feasibility is assessed against isolated CPU standard-library Python without network or credentials; every runtime expansion requires separate review. Conditional limitations are not permanent source exclusions. No source instructions were executed.
linked_reference_caveat: Linked references, companion skills, external documentation, tool behavior, and licenses have not been independently reviewed. Their availability, compatibility, permissions, and licensing must be checked before use. Scrubbed examples are research text, not validated runnable programs.

sources.workflow: Define contracts before implementation; standardize errors and naming, validate external boundaries, add compatible fields, paginate collections, and implement deliberate idempotency semantics with atomic claims, payload matching, in-flight handling, unknown outcomes, and retention.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs the intended API, consumer expectations, input and output types, validation rules, and retry paths. The illustrated TypeScript work needs its compiler and application stack. Idempotency needs a store enforcing uniqueness atomically; real downstream effects and replay windows need the actual integration contract and retention policy.
sources.offline_assessment: Contract design and review are faithful bounded offline work with supplied project facts. A genuinely requested Python implementation could exercise local validation, pagination, and SQLite uniqueness without extra packages; it would not execute the TypeScript examples or establish behavior of a payment provider, distributed retries, production consumers, or a full service. Those concrete operations require separately reviewed runtimes and integrations, not substituted plans or synthetic charges.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently authored contract and compatibility cases should check boundary errors, duplicate concurrency, conflicting payloads, pending and unknown outcomes, and retention against real retry requirements. A separately authorized integration verifier must establish downstream effects; schema inspection alone is insufficient.

sources.workflow: Configure enforced lint, types, tests, build, integration, optional end-to-end, audit, and bundle gates; feed failures back into fixes; establish preview and staged deployments, flags, rollback, secrets separation, reviews, and pipeline optimization.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Examples require a hosted repository and Actions runners, Node 22, npm dependencies and project scripts. Database integration adds PostgreSQL 16, migrations, and CI secrets; browser tests add Playwright and Chromium. Preview deployment requires deployment tooling and a token. Merge enforcement needs repository administration and human approval; staged production rollout needs environments and monitoring.
sources.offline_assessment: Given a project, offline pipeline configuration review or authoring is a real limited deliverable. Standard-library Python cannot demonstrate npm builds, browser execution, hosted event triggers, branch protection, secret storage, audits using current advisories, or deployments. Even package-equipped local checks would not prove hosted enforcement or production rollback. Each expansion needs separate review, and configuration alone cannot satisfy the pipeline-running or under-ten-minute checks.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: A separately authorized verifier must inspect actual hosted run artifacts, inject a failing gate to confirm merge blocking, validate secret isolation, and observe deployment and rollback in an approved test environment. Pipeline duration requires actual timing, not the source's target.

sources.workflow: Discover the existing stack and baseline, interview the user with four defaulted questions, record justified constraints and exceptions, install chosen established checkers, wire lifecycle gates, inspect weakening diffs, and ratchet measured baselines.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Interactive threshold selection requires a live user. The source explicitly allows non-interactive floor-only work with human follow-up. Repository files, branch-point diffs, existing test and coverage outputs, and selected checker commands are needed. Numbered dimensions may require package installations, scanner rules or advisory data, a browser and running app for performance and accessibility, CI hooks, and human ownership.
sources.offline_assessment: Supplied repository snapshots and diffs permit offline floor review and baseline arithmetic; floor-only is an explicit initial path, not grounds to discard the source. Its companion floor-guard reference remains unreviewed. A written constraint is not an enforced one. The default runtime lacks the named third-party checkers, browser measurements, and external data; these need separate review. Defaults and sample coverage numbers cannot be reported as user decisions or measured baselines.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: A human must approve dimensions, exceptions, and the bar. An independent verifier should compare branch-point constraints and tests, try deliberate weakening cases, inspect checker outputs and lifecycle wiring, and verify any claimed external constraint and ratchet from genuine measurements.

sources.workflow: Curate persistent rules, relevant specifications and source, focused failure evidence, and conversation state. Preserve restartable task handoffs, trim stale context, protect current constraints, position active material deliberately, and surface conflicts rather than invent requirements.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs actual project rules, relevant code and tests, specifications, task state, and verification evidence. Restart checks require repository state and an agent harness that can restart or compact; commits require authorization. Optional context integrations need configured documentation, browser, database, filesystem, or repository tools and their access. Unresolved requirements need human decisions.
sources.offline_assessment: Selecting supplied files, drafting context packs, classifying untrusted material, and recording accurate handoffs are faithful offline deliverables. The optional service integrations are not prerequisites for every pack. Standard-library text processing can inspect supplied content, but cannot demonstrate model adherence, context-window effects, session supervision, or authenticated integrations. Those evaluations require separate harness or service review and actual observations; the stated context thresholds are advice, not measured study results.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: A separate reviewer should check that packs and handoffs preserve the original scope, approvals, current files, unresolved questions, and actual test outcomes. Agent-quality and restart-reliability claims require an independently scored harness evaluation, not a well-written rules file.

sources.workflow: Stop changes and preserve evidence; reproduce, localize, minimize, fix the root cause, add a failing-before regression test, and verify the original scenario plus existing tests and build. Use history bisection where relevant and treat diagnostic output as untrusted.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires a concrete failure, expected behavior, source, reproducible inputs, and repository-specific test and build tooling. Regression bisection needs Git and a known-good history point. Browser, database, service, CI, or production incidents additionally need their actual environment and diagnostic evidence; dependency fixes can require installations.
sources.offline_assessment: A supplied deterministic standard-library Python bug can support the real reproduce-fix-regression cycle offline in an isolated writable task copy. Reading logs alone supports triage, not a verified fix. This batch ran nothing. Browser failures, application builds, history bisection, and external-service or production-only failures are not established by Python substitutes; expand the runtime only after review and never treat an unreproduced issue or safe fallback as proof of repair.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: An independent regression test should fail on the original and pass on the fix, with unchanged acceptance criteria, full relevant checks, and reproduction of the original scenario. Intermittent or environment-specific fixes additionally need evidence from the approved representative environment.

sources.workflow: Decide whether deprecation is justified, provide a production-proven replacement and migration support, migrate consumers incrementally, confirm zero active usage, and remove the old system. For databases, expand, dual-write, batch backfill, switch reads, then contract in a later deploy with tested down paths.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs consumer inventory and usage metrics, a working alternative covering critical use cases, maintenance and migration costs, ownership, and advisory or compulsory policy decisions. Actual cutover requires old and new implementations, tests, production evidence, routing or flags, deploy authority, database access, representative data, and reversible migration tooling.
sources.offline_assessment: Inventory analysis and migration guides from supplied facts are bounded offline work. Local Python or SQLite migration operations can establish only their own explicitly scoped semantics, not production readiness, PostgreSQL locking behavior, zero downtime, or that all real consumers migrated. The source explicitly demands production-proven replacement and actual usage evidence for completion. Service, database-engine, and production work requires separate review; neither a plan nor a toy backfill completes that workflow.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: An independent owner must verify consumer coverage and zero active old usage. A separately approved database verifier should test mixed-version compatibility, down paths, data preservation, batching and lock impact on the target engine before any destructive phase; rollback advice is not a guarantee of reversibility.

sources.workflow: Record architectural decisions, alternatives, consequences, and lifecycle status using existing repository conventions; document non-obvious intent and API contracts; maintain accurate setup instructions, changelog, and agent-facing rules.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs actual decisions and their rationale, repository conventions and existing ADR numbering, current code and public contracts, setup commands, and shipped changes. Conflicting conventions or unsettled decisions require human resolution. The template's database and framework choices are examples, not mandatory installations or infrastructure.
sources.offline_assessment: With supplied authoritative project facts, writing and reviewing ADRs, API prose, a README, or changelog is a complete bounded offline documentation task. Standard-library text handling is enough; there is no inherent browser, credential, service, or deployment requirement. However, authoring setup commands does not establish that they run, and the example database comparisons are unverified source claims. Executable quick-start or generated-documentation validation would require the relevant separately reviewed stack.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: A decision owner should confirm rationale and acceptance status; a separate reader should compare contracts, commands, numbering, and changelog entries against repository facts. Any claim that setup instructions execute successfully needs actual clean-environment results, not documentation completeness alone.

sources.workflow: Name a non-trivial claim, extract artifact and contract without the author's reasoning, seek adversarial fresh-context findings, reconcile each finding against the artifact, and stop on trivial findings, three cycles, or user override. Offer cross-model review interactively; skip it explicitly in non-interactive contexts.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Ordinarily needs a main-session orchestrator capable of spawning a fresh-context reviewer, an artifact, an explicit contract, and reconciliation. The source forbids nested persona orchestration and labels self-questioning degraded. Optional external CLI review requires installed working tooling, exact syntax confirmation, authentication as applicable, and authorization for each invocation.
sources.offline_assessment: Artifact extraction and evidence-based reconciliation are offline work. Self-review is not fresh-context review and cannot silently replace it. The source permits a genuinely failing TDD test to satisfy behavioral disproof, so suitable standard-library Python behavior offers a narrower real path if actually tested. No tests or reviewer calls occurred here. Full fresh-context or cross-model execution exceeds the default runtime and needs separate review; skipping cross-model does not itself eliminate the initial review requirement.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: A genuinely independent reviewer or independently judged failing behavioral test must attempt to falsify the contract. Verify reviewer input isolation, actionable reconciliation, and stop conditions. Record degraded self-questioning honestly and do not count it as independent validation.

sources.workflow: Build composed, focused UI components with appropriate state, design-system tokens, reference-led visual decisions, accessible keyboard and focus behavior, responsive layouts, and loading, empty, error, success, and permission states; finish by checking the rendered interface.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs product tasks and content, current components and design tokens, application dependencies and build/runtime tooling, plus references or explicitly recorded design assumptions. React and query-library examples require their real ecosystem if adopted. Final checks require a browser, accessibility tools or assistive technology, specified viewport sizes, and UI-specific review.
sources.offline_assessment: Supplied design systems and screenshots allow offline design-contract and source review. The source explicitly permits unavailable references to be replaced by documented assumptions checked against the existing design system; browsing is not universally required. But standard-library Python cannot execute React components, inspect rendered focus or responsive behavior, establish screen-reader usability, or certify visual polish. Browser and package expansion need separate review, and source markup or screenshot plans cannot stand in for the required rendered finish gate.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: An independent UI reviewer should inspect actual rendering at all four specified widths, exercise keyboard and modal focus, use assistive technology, and check realistic states against the product design contract. Static ARIA attributes or a clean automated scan alone do not prove accessibility.

sources.workflow: Organize short-lived branches and atomic tested commits, separate concerns, inspect staged changes and secrets, use worktrees for parallel streams, and maintain compatible semantic versions, immutable release tags, and curated consumer-facing changelogs.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Actual commit, branch, worktree, bisect, blame, and tag operations require Git, a writable repository with relevant history, author identity and authorization, and project-specific checks. Remote push or pull-request work adds configured remote access and credentials as applicable. Release classification needs consumer compatibility facts and the team's branching and release policy.
sources.offline_assessment: A supplied diff and history export permit bounded offline commit grouping, message drafting, compatibility analysis, and changelog review. Real local Git operations can be offline but Git is outside the stated Python-only runtime and needs review plus an isolated disposable repository. Remote publishing requires additional authorization and service access. Draft messages do not create atomic history; synthetic logs do not verify tags or safe rollback. Destructive reset examples must not be executed against a shared working tree.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Inspect actual resulting commits, parentage, staged scope, ignored files, and independent test evidence in an approved repository copy. A release verifier must compare observable compatibility with the chosen version and match tag, artifact, and changelog; remote publication needs separate confirmation.

sources.workflow: Implement the smallest complete slice, test and verify it, commit, and proceed without restarting completed work. Prefer vertical or risk-first slices, maintain buildability, keep scope tight, use conservative flags where needed, and keep increments independently revertible.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs a scoped feature or plan, acceptance expectations, the actual codebase and test/build/lint/type commands, and Git for required commits. Full-stack slices additionally need their real database, API and UI runtimes. Feature flags and migration rollback apply where relevant; the linked project-wide completion bar is not included in this body.
sources.offline_assessment: A pure standard-library Python feature could support real small implementation and test increments offline in a permitted isolated copy. The documented workflow also requires actual commits, which need a separately reviewed Git expansion. For browser or database features, generating layers or mocking the frontend during contract-first development is only an intermediate slice: final integration still must work. Plans, stub endpoints, and successful unit tests cannot substitute for requested end-to-end behavior or unavailable builds.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: An independent acceptance check should verify each slice's user-visible behavior and inspect recorded test/build results and actual commits. Final verification must exercise the integrated feature and unchanged regressions, not only assess that the slice ordering looks reasonable.

sources.workflow: Define on-call questions, map them to structured logs, bounded RED or USE metrics and distributed traces, propagate correlation and entry-point identity, protect sensitive fields, write actionable symptom alerts and runbooks, then trigger paths and inspect actual telemetry.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs a concrete service and its entry points, dependency boundaries, on-call questions, SLO or historical threshold evidence, and telemetry ownership. Examples use a structured logger, Prometheus client or OpenTelemetry SDK, application integrations, collectors or backends, tracing UI, staging traffic, and a real alert destination.
sources.offline_assessment: A genuinely scoped Python local feature can emit actual structured logs and permit local redaction or correlation checks with standard-library facilities; supplied telemetry can also be analyzed offline. That does not execute the illustrated SDK stack or prove cross-service propagation, queryable backend histograms, delivered alerts, or staging diagnosis. Those parts need separately reviewed packages and isolated services. A runbook is a legitimate artifact but does not satisfy the explicit trigger-and-observe verification.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: An independent operator should induce a controlled failure only in an authorized test environment, locate it by telemetry alone, follow cross-boundary identity, check bounded labels and sensitive-data handling, and confirm test alerts reach the intended channel with a usable runbook.

sources.workflow: Measure a real baseline, identify the bottleneck, make one attributable fix, remeasure under identical conditions against variance and correctness gates, revert neutral or worse attempts, record all attempts, and add synthetic and field regression guards.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires an actual performance problem, representative inputs and conditions, repeatable measurement budget, correctness tests, and an agreed metric. Frontend verification calls for browser profiling plus real-user data; database work needs the actual engine, data and query plans; caching and pooling may need multiple instances or external systems. CI budgets need their named ecosystem tooling.
sources.offline_assessment: For an expressly requested CPU-bound standard-library Python workload, actual repeated local timing and correctness checks could faithfully implement the measurement cycle offline. No such measurements occurred here. Saved traces can support analysis but not a new improvement claim. Python microbenchmarks or SQLite plans cannot establish React rendering, target-database query behavior, production latency, or real-user improvements. Browser, database, cache, field-data, and CI expansions need separate review.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: A verifier should rerun before and after under matched budgets and conditions, compare improvement with measured variance, independently guard required behavior, and inspect reverted-attempt records. User-facing success additionally requires approved representative browser or field evidence; example numbers and source targets are not results.

sources.workflow: Read the spec and relevant code without implementing, map dependencies, write small vertical tasks with acceptance and verification criteria, order risks and checkpoints, and save a plan plus tasks in the designated target without overwriting incomplete unrelated work.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs clear requirements or a spec, repository patterns, dependency facts, existing plan status, and a task-list destination. Local Markdown is the default and requires no issue-tracker service. A designated external tracker adds its integration and access. Conflicting incomplete plans require human resolution, and the final checklist explicitly requires human plan approval.
sources.offline_assessment: A concrete plan and dependency-ordered task list are the requested output here, not substitutes for implementation, so supplied project facts support faithful offline authoring with no packages or builds. Commands listed for future verification need not be executed merely to plan, but cannot be reported as passed. External tracker creation exceeds the default runtime, and human approval cannot be fabricated. Those conditions need separate review or a genuine human decision; implementation is outside this workflow.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: A separate reviewer should compare task coverage and acceptance criteria with the spec, check dependency order and checkpoints, and ensure existing incomplete work was preserved. Record actual human approval separately from an automatically generated plan; tracker tasks require evidence of real creation if that target was requested.

sources.workflow: Clear code, security, performance, accessibility, infrastructure and documentation gates; prepare flags and rollback; deploy to staging and production incrementally; compare canary metrics over stated observation windows; respect the error budget and verify health, critical flows, telemetry and rollback readiness.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires a built and tested application, reviewed code, dependency audits, browser and accessibility evidence where applicable, production configuration and infrastructure, database migrations, monitoring baselines, team coordination, and authorized staging and production access. The rollout specifies day-scale monitoring and a week after full rollout, plus user traffic and business metrics.
sources.offline_assessment: An explicitly requested launch checklist, readiness analysis, rollout policy, or rollback document can be produced offline from supplied evidence. Actual shipping is not achievable in isolated Python without services or credentials, and cannot be replaced by an imagined deployment or synthetic health response. Build, audit, browser, infrastructure, production, and long-duration monitoring each require separate review. A local rehearsal can only establish that rehearsal, never completion of the stated production launch.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: An authorized release owner must verify genuine gate artifacts, deployment identity, canary-versus-baseline metrics, monitoring windows, error-budget state, manual critical flows, and executable rollback readiness. Independently validate example rollback commands against the actual platform rather than trusting their presence in the source.

sources.workflow: Detect exact project versions, retrieve the specific authoritative documentation, extract version-specific API facts while rejecting embedded directives, implement documented patterns, cite the supporting evidence, surface conflicts, and explicitly flag unverifiable patterns.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs dependency manifests with unambiguous versions, relevant official documentation and compatibility information, project code, and the real framework runtime for checking that patterns work. Missing versions or conflicting project conventions require user decisions. Its normal retrieval step requires documentation access; source citation completeness needs the actual authoritative content.
sources.offline_assessment: If exact-version official documentation and project facts are supplied locally with trustworthy provenance, bounded offline evidence extraction and source-backed implementation may be possible for a compatible target. That does not establish current online guidance or satisfy a specifically requested new fetch. The eighteen skill bodies are not the linked framework documentation. Default Python cannot execute arbitrary framework examples, and this batch neither fetched nor ran anything. Retrieval and framework runtimes require separate review; memory or invented citations cannot replace missing documentation.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: A verifier should independently match each substantive API claim and implementation to the detected version and supplied authoritative passage, check provenance and compatibility, and exercise behavior in the approved target runtime. Flag unresolved conflicts and missing evidence instead of treating citations as executable proof.

sources.workflow: Discover repository-specific testing commands, write and observe a failing behavioral test, implement the minimum fix, refactor while green, and run the relevant full suite. Prefer outcome checks and real code, reproduce bugs before fixing, and add browser runtime checks when browser behavior is involved.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs concrete expected behavior, source under change, the repository's actual test framework and wrappers, and repeatable inputs. Small tests use one process without external resources; integrations require their local dependencies, and browser behavior requires a real browser and DevTools integration. Complex-bug independent test authorship is an optional agent-assisted path.
sources.offline_assessment: For genuine standard-library Python code and tests, the actual red-green-refactor cycle can run offline without third-party packages or services. This batch executed no cycle. The source is not inherently restricted to TypeScript. Existing projects using other runners require separately reviewed tooling; local database or browser integration adds further runtime requirements. Fakes may isolate a boundary as the source allows, but cannot count as real end-to-end service success, and writing a plausible failing test without running it is not RED.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: An independent behavioral test or assessor should verify that the reproduction fails for the intended reason before the fix and passes afterward, without weakened assertions or skipped cases. Inspect full relevant suite results and actual browser evidence for browser tasks; an agent-authored green suite alone is not proof.

sources.workflow: Classify the task by development phase, select applicable skills, surface assumptions and unresolved conflicts, keep implementation simple and scoped, and demand actual per-skill verification plus the project-wide completion bar. Choose only the lifecycle stages relevant to the task.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs a concrete task, the available skill catalogue and full applicable skill bodies, project rules and specifications, and access to the actual verification evidence. Missing requirements need human resolution. Invoking a selected workflow inherits its particular tools, packages, browser, repository, credentials, service, or production prerequisites; the full referenced completion bar and several named skills are not in this batch.
sources.offline_assessment: A bounded routing decision with rationale can be performed offline from supplied task and skill texts without executing the chosen workflow. Standard-library tooling can inspect a local catalogue but cannot demonstrate agent compliance or run every downstream stage. The source explicitly says not every task needs every skill, so no universal deployment or credential requirement follows from this meta-skill. Actual invocation and completion must be separately reviewed and evidenced, not reported from a proposed sequence.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: An independent assessor should compare routing with the real request and available skill definitions, verify unresolved assumptions were not silently resolved, and inspect the chosen workflow's actual acceptance evidence. Do not equate selecting a skill or reciting its checklist with completing it.

source_reader: Delegated complete-original-body review; exact cohort selection, original hashes, line totals, disjoint IDs and citation bounds independently reconciled by parent.
status_scope: Only original-body prerequisites; linked references, concrete tasks and runtime evidence remain distinct.
